text: Every small business has this list. Invoices that went out weeks ago, still unpaid. The hard part isn't the money. It's deciding who to chase, and what to say.
This is Pay Pilot, an A I receivables assistant built on PayPal Invoicing. Everything here is live: real PayPal Sandbox calls, running on Azure. No real money moves.
Here's my overview. Four thousand and fifty dollars outstanding, across three invoices. Two thousand and fifty of it is already overdue.

And before I've asked anything, it's ranked them. Twelve hundred dollars, twelve days late, score seventy nine. Each score has a plain English reason. It's a heuristic, not machine learning, and it says so.
These are real Sandbox invoices from the PayPal Invoicing A P I. PayPal's own status sits under Pay Pilot's overdue math, so you can check its work.
Now let me just ask it. Which invoices are a week or more overdue, and which should I chase first?
Watch the tool calls. It isn't guessing from a prompt stuffed with numbers. It calls typed tools, a summary, then the overdue analysis, and answers only from what they return.
Two invoices, two thousand and fifty dollars. Chase the twelve hundred first. Same answer as the dashboard, because it's the same scoring code underneath.
So. Draft a friendly reminder for that one.
This is the part I care about most. The agent can write a draft. It cannot send one. There is no send tool for it to call. The draft goes into an approval queue, and it stops there.
And here it is. Recipient, amount, twelve days overdue, and why it picked this invoice. Nothing has been sent.
I'll add a line of my own, because it's my customer.
Approve, and send. Only now does the server re-check the invoice with PayPal, and then call the reminder endpoint.
H T T P two oh four. PayPal accepted it. One honest caveat: PayPal sends its own template and ignores custom text. So my note is kept here for the record, not emailed.
Now the other direction. Inside PayPal, I've just recorded a payment on the two thousand dollar invoice that's due tomorrow. I haven't touched Pay Pilot.
PayPal fires a webhook. Pay Pilot verifies the signature with PayPal, stores the event exactly once, and refreshes the invoice. There it is: invoice paid, PayPal verified.
And that's the whole trail. The A I draft, my approval, PayPal's two oh four, and the payment. Each one labelled with where it came from.
Back on the overview. Outstanding is down to two thousand and fifty. Paid this month, two thousand one hundred and twenty five.
Pay Pilot. The A I does the reading, the ranking, and the writing. A person makes every call that reaches a customer.
